instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of the basmati rice in a fine strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Transfer it to a medium saucepan with 2 1/4 cups water and a pinch of salt. Bring it to a boil over high heat, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 5 minutes, then fluff it with a fork.

Meanwhile, finely chop the onion and keep 1/3 cup of it for the omelette. Mince the ginger and garlic. Chop the tomatoes. Chop 3 tbsp of the cilantro for the omelette, and the rest for the end. Slice the green chili thin and set it in a small bowl for the table.
In a bowl, whisk the eggs with the 1/3 cup onion, 3 tbsp cilantro and 1/2 tsp of the salt until well mixed.

Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a 10 inch nonstick skillet with a lid over medium high heat for 1 minute. Pour in the egg mixture and turn the heat to its lowest setting. Cover and cook for 8 minutes, until the underside is set and the top is only just moist.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds. After about 20 seconds they will sizzle and smell toasty.
Add the remaining onion and cook for 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until golden brown.
Add the ginger and garlic and stir for 1 minute. Add the turmeric, chili powder, coriander and garam masala and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Cook for 6 minutes, stirring often, until they're soft and the oil shows at the edges of the masala.
Add 1 1/2 cups water and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat to medium low and simmer for 5 minutes.

Slide the omelette onto a large plate, then flip it back into the skillet with the browned side up. Cook it uncovered over low heat for 2 minutes. Transfer it to a cutting board and cut it into 2 inch pieces.
Turn the heat under the gravy to low. Add the omelette pieces and spoon the gravy over them. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Take the skillet off the heat and scatter over the rest of the cilantro.
Taste the gravy. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve over the rice, with the sliced green chili on the side.
method_notes: No version of this dish has 20 ratings with a score of 4.0 or better, and none of the trusted Indian cooks has one, so this leads with My Tasty Curry (5 from 8), the only rated version: a thick spiced omelette cooked low under a lid, cut up and added to a tomato masala at the end. Blogexplore, Foods and Flavors and Playful Cooking roll thin omelettes or add potatoes instead. Quantities are scaled up by half for four with rice, and the gravy takes the page's body-text 1 cup of water and more, so it's a real sauce rather than a few spoonfuls. The green chili is left out of the omelette and sliced at the table to keep the pot mild. It comes in at about 34 minutes.
